claims.statement: Page metadata lists fpt, ghec and ghes, but billing and feature applicability depend on conditional body branches. The introduction describes charges beyond included minutes/storage; it is not an estate billing observation.

The fpt/ghec include says standard GitHub-hosted runners in public repositories and self-hosted runners are free; private hosted use receives plan-dependent minutes/storage and excess is billed. The GHES else branch describes free Actions usage on self-hosted runners. Larger-runner exceptions remain in the separate larger-runners page.
In fpt/ghec, Actions is available across GitHub products except private repositories owned by legacy per-repository-plan accounts. The linked plan page is not imported as a new reviewed source.

Hosted-runner usage limits are linked rather than enumerated here. The source requires use within GitHub Terms of Service and references additional Actions product terms; these linked legal bodies were not cleared or adopted by this review.

In fpt/ghec, organization owners and users with View organization Actions metrics permission may view usage. The include warns displayed usage minutes exclude minute multipliers and primarily describe where/how usage occurs; they are not billing totals.
Reusable-workflow billing is always associated with the caller. Hosted-runner assignment uses only the caller context; the caller cannot use hosted runners from the called repository.
Usage and retention policies can be managed at repository, organization and enterprise scopes. The four configuration links are navigation references, not reviewed configurations or executed changes.
